confounds: Diagnosed users were more active on average, with about 649 retained posts per user versus 530 for controls; full-timeline any-match prevalence and persistence therefore remain activity-sensitive.
The label distribution was highly imbalanced: 619 diagnosed versus 5,463 control users.
First-person detection was heuristic; quotation, lyrics, jokes, news, advocacy, and third-person discussion cannot be perfectly separated with lexical rules.
Source order was available but dates were not, so ten-bin persistence measures spread across the retained timeline rather than duration or recurrence over calendar time.
Observed topic differences may reflect demographic, age, gender, fandom, lifestyle, or collection differences rather than symptoms.
Therapy, medication, and diagnosis terms may reflect ascertainment or annotation processes rather than latent depression severity.
Portuguese slang, negation, irony, code-switching, and spelling variation limit lexical precision; these results are corpus associations, not clinical measurements.

caveats: Lexical sadness includes transient distress and references to other people.
First-person, quotation, and third-person markers are heuristic and can co-occur.
findings.evidence_summary: Sadness and crying were common but consistently more prevalent among diagnosed users. Sadness matches had first-person proxies in roughly 58% of diagnosed versus 44% of control matched posts; quotation markers were about equal.
findings.prompt_guidance: Prefer repeated, self-referential sadness or crying combined with other symptoms over isolated emotional words.

negative_results: Punishment/deservingness language did not generalize: precise punishment terms favored diagnosed users in only 2/4 folds (14.4% vs 16.2% overall).
Reduced-libido language was extremely rare (0.8% diagnosed vs 0.2% control), lacked persistence, and was not stable across folds.
Explicit self-failure was weak after disambiguation (16.5% vs 14.7%; 3/4 folds); broad inability wording was inflated by ordinary tasks, sleep, and choices.
Generic sleep, concentration, and irritability mentions were high-base-rate and weakly separated. Generic sleep occurred for 94.5% diagnosed vs 90.3% control.
Pessimism showed only modest user-level separation and no post-rate separation (0.179% diagnosed vs 0.181% control); one fold reversed direction.
Strict self-dislike was rare (3.9% vs 2.0%); self-criticism, worthlessness, and guilt were stronger signals.
